assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction in the transmission electron microscope is a clean invention that took atomic-resolution imaging and spectroscopy below the angstrom scale and changed how interfaces, defects, oxides and catalysts are studied across materials physics. From my own microscopy practice the impact is routine and field-wide, which is the lasting-impact test for a discovery or invention.
assessment.attribution: The decisive chain is Rose's theoretical design of the multipole corrector, Haider's engineering realization of a working corrector for the TEM, and Urban's demonstration and application at sub-angstrom resolution. This maps naturally onto a three-person prize. Other important contributors, for example in the STEM corrector line, are not in the supplied credit list and I cannot resolve that boundary from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Correctors have been commercial for roughly two decades and independently reproduced in many laboratories; the interpretation is entirely stable and recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the STEM corrector development is adequately covered by the supplied names is unresolved.
I have not independently verified the current status of every credited person, which could affect eligibility.
Committee may judge this an instrumentation prize in a field recently recognised (electron microscopy in chemistry, and attosecond tools), so field balance is an open question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene, followed by correlated insulating and superconducting states, opened moire quantum matter as a tunable platform and spawned a large and original field. Few recent discoveries combine a precise theoretical prediction with a striking experimental confirmation.
assessment.attribution: MacDonald and Bistritzer made the decisive theoretical prediction of the magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the experimental discovery of correlated and superconducting phases. A two-person prize of theory plus experiment is fair; Bistritzer's role is genuine but I judge MacDonald the principal theory voice. The early-career experimental first author is not in the supplied list, which complicates the experimental side.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups reproduce the phenomena, but the nature of the superconducting pairing and sample-dependence remain active questions, so it is somewhat early for a final judgement on lasting consequences.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism in the superconducting phase is not settled.
Sample-to-sample variation and twist-angle disorder complicate interpretation.
Credit split between Bistritzer and MacDonald, and the unlisted experimental co-discoverers, is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, gives fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and underpins a redefinition of the second, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy. It is a clear invention with direct, quantifiable performance.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and realized early clocks; Jun Ye brought the system to record accuracy and many-body-controlled operation. Two laureates is a coherent configuration, though other optical-clock groups (ion clocks, frequency combs) have been recognised or may claim parts.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories operate lattice clocks and international comparisons confirm the performance; maturity is high.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier frequency-comb and ion-clock prizes may make the committee view the field as already recognised.
Relative weight of Katori's conceptual proposal and Ye's performance advances is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy spins at room temperature created solid-state quantum sensing, with nanoscale magnetometry and thermometry used in materials physics and biology. It is original and has real consequences for measuring local properties in solids.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko demonstrated optical detection of single NV centres and coherent control, which is the decisive step. Lukin and others contributed important quantum-information and sensing proposals and demonstrations; I would not include more than two on the evidence supplied, but the boundary with the sensing applications is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Strong, widely reproduced experimentally; applications are still maturing, so recognition is plausible but less settled than for the established instrumentation candidates.
uncertainties: The line between the discovery of single-spin control and later sensing applications is unclear.
Credit for Lukin's contributions against the two experimentalists is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics provides strong coupling of superconducting artificial atoms to microwave photons and is the architecture of leading superconducting quantum processors. The idea and its realization are original and highly influential.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and collaborators proposed cQED and Schoelkopf's group realized strong coupling and readout; this supports a three-person prize. Note that superconducting-circuit quantum physics has recently received a prize, so the committee would need to argue for distinct novelty.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed in many laboratories and strongly consolidated, though the technological payoff is still unfolding.
uncertainties: Possible recency of a recent prize in superconducting circuits may weigh against it.
Full list of key experimental contributors beyond the supplied names cannot be verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and later association with a blazar and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy as a new window on the universe, a discovery in the strict sense of the prize.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the conception and realization of the cubic-kilometre detector, with Karle and Spiering as senior figures. Credit for a large collaboration is difficult to compress to three names and the supplied credit does not resolve this; pioneers of earlier neutrino telescope efforts are also relevant.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed by multiple analyses and source associations are accumulating, but source identification remains incomplete.
uncertainties: Collaboration scale makes individual attribution contentious.
Source population is only partially identified, so interpretation continues to evolve.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators, and its experimental confirmation in HgTe quantum wells, established a new class of materials with protected edge and surface states. The idea is original and has changed the way solids are classified.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the foundational theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental observation (with the Zhang theoretical proposal for HgTe not included in this list). A theory-plus-experiment pair is attractive, but credit among Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and others is not represented in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many experiments, with materials-science consequences, though technological use is limited so far and prior topological prizes may be seen as overlapping.
uncertainties: Credit omitted from the supplied names (HgTe theory proposal, 3D topological insulators) complicates a fair configuration.
Overlap with the 2016 topological phases prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard-type models with controllable parameters, giving quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter, including the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition and quantum gas microscopy. This is original and conceptually clear.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch) proposed the Hubbard realization; Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott-insulator experiments and microscopy; Esslinger's fermionic work is also decisive but cannot fit within three. The four-person candidate forces a difficult omission.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by several groups; the simulation programme is still developing, so the decisive impact on understanding real materials is not yet established.
uncertainties: Four serious contributors compete for three places.
Practical utility for materials problems remains open.
